label: rem:information-causality
title: Information causality and the light cone
html:
One places the quantum observable universe (QOU) within information-theoretic physics. The energy \mathfrak{E} = \mathfrak{m}\,c_q^2 (energy) and the derived speed of light c_q = 1/(q-1) connect the QOU to established information bounds.

1. The light cone is the Lieb--Robinson cone. The causal boundary arises from the q-connection decomposition A_q = q^{-1}A + \hbar_q\iota_\xi A\varTheta. The boundary at |Z| = c_q in the contact affine coordinate (contact affine chart) is the locus where horizontal spatial diffusion matches vertical Reeb advance. Outside this cone, the Lieb--Robinson bound enforces exponential suppression of correlations. Causality follows directly from the ratio of spatial to temporal information flow.

2. The speed of light varies with q. The speed of light c_q = 1/(q-1) depends on the substrate parameter. At the Big Bang (q \to \infty), c \to 0. As the universe classicalises (q \to 1), c \to \infty. At the present epoch q = q_0, c \approx 9.093 in Reeb units.

3. The Margolus--Levitin bound and c_q. The Margolus--Levitin theorem of Norman Margolus and Lev B. Levitin [margolus1998] bounds the orthogonal-state transition rate by 2\mathfrak{E}/\pi\hbar [lloyd2000]. One has the energy \mathfrak{E} = \mathfrak{m}\,c_q^2 = \mathfrak{m}/(q-1)^2 and the operation count n_R(q) = 1/\hbar_q. The bound is:

  n_R(q)  \leq  \frac{2\mathfrak{m}}{\pi\hbar_q(q-1)^2}.

The Reeb dynamics saturates this bound up to the factor 2/\pi.

4. Bremermann's limit and information bandwidth. Bremermann's limit, evaluated as a mass-energy ceiling on physical computation by Seth Lloyd [lloyd2000], states that a system processes at most mc^2/h bits per second. The bandwidth is:

  \mathfrak{B}(q)
  =  \frac{q\eta_q}{(q-1)^2}
  \quad \text{(\(q\)-bits per Planck time)}.

At q = q_0, \mathcal{B} \approx 82 q-bits per Planck time.

5. Pawlowski's information causality. Information causality [pawlowski2009] restricts the accessible information Bob gains from Alice. In the QOU, the Lieb--Robinson bound ensures exponential decay outside the |Z| = c_q cone.

6. The Bekenstein bound and fibre entropy. The Bekenstein bound of Jacob D. Bekenstein [bekenstein1981] limits the entropy to S \leq 2\pi RE / \hbar c. One bounds the QOU fibre entropy by \eta_q per operation:

  S_{\mathrm{fibre}}  \leq  \eta_q
  =  \frac{2q - 1}{q^3}.

7. Summary. Every classical information and computation bound above [lloyd2000] descends from two substrate quantities: the causal cone |Z| = c_q with c_q = 1/(q-1), and the per-operation fibre-entropy ceiling \eta_q = (2q - 1)/q^3. The cone fixes the Lieb--Robinson / information-causality light cone and the q-dependent speed of light; the entropy ceiling caps the Margolus--Levitin operation rate, the Bremermann bandwidth \mathfrak{B}(q), and the Bekenstein entropy. Causality, processing rate, and entropy are thus one q-parametrised family.
